review_reference: Owner decision of 2026-11-10, relayed by Ola (clinical owner), for 0120 (Access PIN): "a PIN gives exactly 24 hours of read AND write access to all records, with no separate 'Ask for more access'", for the same staff roles as today; the backend goes live first, then the website. Written as 0121 and renumbered 0120 by the release order on 2026-11-11, after hid-system#206 went live, on staging 51d6937a (0001-0114). Unsigned: the owner's 0121 signing of 2026-11-10 is cleared by the renumber and reviewed_by is empty until the owner signs again under 0120 (the plain-English declaration for the owner is in the pull request).
evidence: Single migration 0120_patient_access_pin_day_read_write.sql, written as 0121 and renumbered 0120 by the release order on 2026-11-11; unsigned until the owner signs under 0120 (reviewed_by is empty; the 0121 signing of 2026-11-10 is cleared). BASE: staging a710205f, migrations 0001-0116 (117 files; 0115 and 0116, hid-system#232, landed there on 2026-11-12); 0117-0119 are still missing there (0117 hid-system#218, 0118 and 0119 hid-system#237, on their branches), so the release checks that need a contiguous list fail with "missing migration prefix" until they land. The file differs from the 0121 file only in its number, messages, temporary names, comments and the body md5 it pins; inside the function body only in its two comments that named the number (they said 0121 and say 0120 since 2026-11-13, changed while this declaration was unsigned), so the body's md5 is no longer the 0121 file's (md5 below). WHAT IT DOES: (a) access_requests_pin_scope_ck and consent_grants_pin_scope_ck (0033) allow scope read_records or write_records for a row whose authorization_method is patient_access_pin (still purpose direct-care and break_glass false); each dropped and added NOT VALID, then VALIDATE CONSTRAINT. (b) CREATE OR REPLACE of identity.access_patient_with_pin(text,text,integer) from 0098's body (md5 830c1baa4bca3df57cc02b7b002a8831 before, 60776067ac4f8fad8b34c7f25cb45a89 after): every grant lasts exactly 1440 minutes (24 hours), whatever duration is asked (owner decision of 2026-11-10); the argument requested_duration_minutes is kept, so old and new callers both work, and is still checked as 5-1440 (was 5-60), a missing or out-of-range value refused as before; the access request's requested_duration_minutes and the audit's duration_minutes say 1440, a replay's audit too (the reused grant keeps its own 24-hour expiry); the request and grant it inserts are write_records (was read_records); a still-valid PIN grant is reused only if write_records (an older read_records PIN grant is not reused and is left to run out); a deny directive stops it if its actions are empty or include read_records or write_records (was read_records only); the success and replay audit details and the PatientAccessPinVerified payload carry scope. Every other line is 0098's; signature, result, owner, plpgsql, VOLATILE, SECURITY DEFINER, search_path identity, auth, audit, platform, pg_temp and ACL (hid_identity_runtime and hid_schema_test_runtime EXECUTE) are unchanged and compared attribute by attribute after. (c) identity_outbox_minimum_necessary (0033) accepts a PatientAccessPinVerified payload of {consentGrantId, reviewRequired} or {consentGrantId, reviewRequired, scope} with scope read_records or write_records (EmergencyAccessActivated unchanged); dropped and added NOT VALID, then validated. (d) ALTER POLICY identity_outbox_patient_access_pin_insert (0033): the grant may be read_records or write_records and the payload's scope, when present, must be the grant's; name, command, permissive and roles unchanged. No table, column, index, trigger, role, permission or grant change; runtime-grants.sql unchanged (the file is staging a710205f's, sha256 e0d3c6c6a12cf15207fb575f1a919cd1883c69577233cf6dab5aaf5aec598232, so it is not declared here); no row written. BACKWARD COMPATIBLE: identity-api reads the same result columns; today's image sends 15 or the caller's 5-60 and keeps working (the grant is then write_records for 24 hours, whatever it asks); the new identity-api (same pull request) asks for 1440 by default and accepts 5-1440, and the database always gives 1440. The event dispatcher and notification worker change that accepts both the two-key and the three-key PIN notice is a separate pull request (hid-system#206, branch claude/fervent-galileo-datz4t-pin-notice-scope, no migration) that must be merged and released before 0120 (hid-system#206 is live since 2026-11-11; release order: hid-system#206 first, then 0120 with identity-api, hid-system#208, then hid-system#207 and health#197): a release carrying a migration applies it before rolling out the services (scripts/production_deployment.py), and a PIN notice raised before the new services run would be refused by the old check and not retried. The websites (hid-system apps/web, hid-system#207, and health's staff site, health#197) keep working and change their words and duration after 0120 is live; until then a PIN used there gives write_records for 24 hours though the site asks 60 minutes and its words are out of date.
